platform_scope: Windows only. Hidden behavioural suite: verifier/tests/test_wcancel_semantics.py.

conditions.statement: cancel(request) stops exactly the named pending request: a second request submitted on the same handle is still pending afterwards and later completes with the bytes that were written; cancellation also takes effect when it is issued from a different thread.
conditions.windows_mechanism: CancelIoEx(handle, OVERLAPPED*) -- per-request cancellation that may be issued from any thread -- versus CancelIo, which only covers the calling thread's requests on that handle and still reports success when it cancels nothing

conditions.statement: A request that received a cancellation ends with status 'cancelled' (never an ordinary I/O failure), and cancelling a request that has already completed -- or cancelling the same request twice -- reports failure instead of claiming success.
conditions.windows_mechanism: GetOverlappedResult reporting ERROR_OPERATION_ABORTED (995) for an aborted request and ERROR_NOT_FOUND (1168) when the request is no longer outstanding

conditions.statement: Submitting against an object that was not opened for overlapped I/O is rejected as unsupported instead of silently degrading to a synchronous read.
conditions.windows_mechanism: the kernel object's own mode: a handle opened without FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED cannot carry outstanding requests, which is observable through the object's file mode / completion behaviour rather than through the candidate's own report

conditions.statement: cancel_all(handle) is the only entry point allowed to stop every request submitted by this module and answers with how many it stopped; unusable handles and parameters are classified as badarg, and waiting past a deadline is classified as timeout.
conditions.windows_mechanism: CancelIoEx issued once per outstanding OVERLAPPED on the handle, plus wait deadlines driven by WaitForSingleObject on the per-request completion event

conditions.statement: The public surface keeps its names and signatures, a normal (uncancelled) request still yields a completion carrying the bytes that were written, and the visible smoke suite keeps passing.
conditions.windows_mechanism: the whole cancellation API remains reachable and usable from a plain Python process against real Windows objects
